title: Component rationalization and Auto Layout normalization for buttons, tables, and charts
creator: Priya Patel
description: Goal: Reduce component surface area and bring library Auto Layout rules into a consistent, predictable state for buttons, tables, and charts so developers can rely on stable tokens and minimal variant branching. Scope: - Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost): rationalize into 1 base frame + semantic states rather than many size-based variants. - Tables: normalize row spacing, header/footer padding, and responsive collapse rules using consistent Auto Layout axes. - Charts: align margin/gutter tokens and simplify variant states (with/without legend, compact/regular). Out of scope: new visual refresh or color token changes (handled in separate ticket).
tasks: Audit current Figma components: enumerate variants, overrides, and orphan instances
Define canonical component anatomy for buttons, tables, charts (frames, children, spacing tokens)
Create migration plan for instances: automated renames + manual review list
Implement Auto Layout normalization in working file and run instance fixes
Update design tokens mapping (spacing, radii, font-sizes) and document changes
Run internal design review and handoff with Eng for implementation edge cases
Publish canary library, collect feedback from 3 product teams, then publish stable
acceptance_criteria: Button library exposes one base component per semantic intent with size props, and removed duplicate size-only variants
Tables align to spacing.scale tokens and responsive collapse documented in component spec
Chart components use standard margins/gutter tokens and include examples for legend placement
Auto Layout rules use explicit axes and pinned children (no mixed-frame hacks)
Migration script or checklist reduces manual instance fixes to <20% of current manual workload
Canary publish completed and at least two product teams verified their pages render without layout regressions
